column6: The back-translation alters the terms 'doctrines' to 'principles' and 'convince' to 'assure,' which may shift the emphasis from a focus on belief to a more general assurance of faith. Additionally, 'walk of faith' is simplified to just 'faith,' which could change the intended depth of the relationship with Christ.
column7: The teachings in this book are meant to educate and encourage you, the reader, in the foundational doctrines of the New Testament church. It is my hope that these beliefs will convince and inspire your walk of faith to plant deep roots in Christ and to come to know Him personally.
column8: The teachings of this book are intended to instruct and encourage you, the reader, in the foundational principles of the New Testament church. It is my hope that this faith will assure and inspire you to put down deep roots in Christ and to know Him personally.

column6: The back-translation simplifies the term 'The Scriptures' to 'Scripture,' but does not alter the overall meaning or intent, as both refer to sacred texts.

The back-translation maintains the same conceptual meaning as the original, simply rephrasing 'The Teachings of the Church' to 'The Church’s Teachings' without altering the doctrinal content or intent.
